mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Chinese Notary Public, then Hague Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China (since China is a member of the Apostille Convention; no consular legalization required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Chinese Notary Public, then Hague Apostille by MFA China; parallel path only, no consular legalization

Notarization by Chinese Notary Public, then Hague Apostille by MFA China; no consular legalization chain

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and China's domestic sanctions list (MOFCOM). PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates, with enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily), and upon any trigger event. Results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years. For Taiwan nexus, additional screening against Taiwan's FSC AML database and cross-strait financial intelligence sharing protocols is mandatory. Any positive hit requires immediate suspension of incorporation and filing of a suspicious transaction report (STR) with the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMLMAC).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and SAMR Online Name Clearance Portal (https://www.gsxt.gov.cn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE name must be in Chinese characters, with mandatory four-tier structure: [Administrative Division] + [Distinctive Name] + [Industry/Scope] + [Enterprise Type]. English name is optional but must be a phonetic transliteration of the Chinese name, not a direct translation. For Taiwan-related entities, the Chinese name must not imply sovereignty or political status. All names must be in simplified Chinese characters; traditional Chinese is prohibited.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan: Articles 1, 18, 98-101, 108, 128, 129 and 172; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; Regulations on Permission of Foreign Investment; Tax Registration under the Business Tax Act and the Income Tax Act for profit-seeking enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (MOEA) through the One-Stop Corporate Registration System; foreign investment approval governed by the Investment Commission of MOEA
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Taiwan Company Registration Application for Limited Liability Company (Company Incorporation Registration Form) together with the Articles of Incorporation and the resolutions of the first directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required under the Company Act for a limited company, and no blocked escrow account is imposed by the registry. However, the foreign investment amount approved by the Investment Commission must be remitted through banking channels into the Company's Taiwan bank account and verified by a licensed CPA capital verification report before the company registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-forma First Board of Directors Resolution of CN WFOE LTD, the Company. Whereas the Company is to be incorporated under the Company Act of Taiwan as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company for the purpose of conducting electronic catalog retail of industrial maintenance hardware under ISIC 4791; whereas the sole founding shareholder has submitted the proposed Articles of Incorporation to the first meeting of the board and now wishes to formally subscribe for the paid-in capital, establish the bank mandate, adopt the registered office, and appoint the statutory officers necessary for company registration; and whereas the directors have considered the foreign investment approval, the capital contribution schedule, the B2B MRO e-commerce operating plan, and the payment rails consisting of credit card and SWIFT wire settlement. Now therefore, be it resolved as follows: 1. The Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting are adopted in their entirety and are directed to be filed with the Department of Commercial Affairs of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. The foreign shareholder's subscription of the full paid-in capital in the amount stated in the Contribution Schedule is approved, and management is directed to remit the subscribed capital into the Company's Taiwan bank account, procure a certified public accountant capital verification report, and cause such report to be filed with the registration authority. 2. The registered office of the Company shall be established at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, which address is hereby adopted as the statutory seat for service of process, registry correspondence, tax notices, and corporate records, and the officers are authorized to execute any lease or landlord consent documents required for that office. 3. The Company shall open and maintain deposit, e-commerce settlement, and SWIFT wire accounts with a commercial bank in Taiwan. The general manager, the financial controller, and the compliance officer are appointed as authorized signatories. Any two of such signatories must execute all wire transfers, credit card merchant agreements, and payment instructions in excess of board-set thresholds; below such thresholds, either the general manager or the financial controller may act. All banking documents are ratified prospectively. 4. The following persons are elected and appointed to the statutory offices set opposite their names: the representative director and general manager, the financial controller, and the compliance and anti-money laundering officer. Each such person accepts office and is authorized to sign the registration forms, tax forms, bank forms, and associated attestations. The board also appoints a statutory supervisor to the extent required by the Company Act. 5. All lawful actions taken by the organizers before this resolution, including applying for foreign investment approval, engaging accountants and counsel, and incurring reasonable formation expenses, are ratified. 6. This resolution may be executed in counterparts and takes effect as a single binding corporate act upon adoption by the required majority of the first board of directors. Adopted on the date set forth in the Company records by unanimous written consent of the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval from the Investment Commission of MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (foreign investment review window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the foreign investment approval application to the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs in Taiwan. The application must identify the foreign corporate investor, the proposed wholly foreign-owned limited company, the approved business scope, and the amount of investment. Include the investor's certificate of incorporation, good-standing certificate, ultimate beneficial ownership statement, source-of-funds evidence, power of attorney to the Taiwanese representative, and a business plan describing the ISIC 4791 electronic catalog retail of industrial maintenance hardware and B2B MRO e-commerce activities. The Commission will check negative-list restrictions and issue a letter of permission that controls the maximum capital and shareholding structure. This letter becomes the primary statutory prerequisite for all subsequent corporate registration and bank remittance.
required_dossiers: Investment Application Form
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation and good standing
Ultimate beneficial owner and source of funds declaration
Investment approval power of attorney
Business plan for ISIC 4791 electronic catalog retail of industrial MRO supplies
Passport copies of the proposed representative and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commission issues a deficiency notice, the applicant must file a complete response within 15 working days. If the application is suspended or rejected, the investor may file a petition for administrative appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of receipt, and may also submit a revised application with amended capital amount and scope before filing the appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA - Business Name and Scope Pre-Approval System (One-Stop Corporate Registration Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the investment permit is issued, apply for pre-approval of the company name and line of business before any bank or registration filing. The applicant shall submit in the formal applicant language the proposed legal name of the entity and the exact business-scope description corresponding to ISIC 4791, namely electronic catalog retail of industrial maintenance hardware and B2B MRO e-commerce. The registry will verify that no identical or confusingly similar name exists and that the scope matches the Taiwan standard industrial classification codes. The pre-approval certificate should list up to three acceptable names and can be used later in the bank account opening. The applicant must act within the validity period of the pre-approval certificate.
required_dossiers: Company name and business scope pre-approval application
Foreign investment approval letter
Power of attorney of responsible person
Proposed Articles of Incorporation excerpt
Passport or ID of the representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected because of a conflict, the applicant may immediately select an alternate name from the list or file a new name application; the registry normally issues a provisional decision within 2 days. For unclear business-scope mapping, the applicant may request a scope-code interpretation opinion from the Department of Commercial Affairs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Capital Remittance, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Appointed Taiwan commercial bank and a certified public accountant licensed under the Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the pre-approved company name at a Taiwan commercial bank and present the foreign investment permit, name pre-approval certificate, draft articles of incorporation and responsible officer identification. Remit the approved foreign currency capital into the account using the bank's inbound remittance and foreign-exchange settlement procedures. The bank will issue a foreign exchange settlement certificate and a receipt of inward remittance after clearing. Engage a licensed CPA to review the remittance evidence, bank statement, investment permit and articles of incorporation, and to issue a formal capital verification report. This report is mandatory for the final company registration; the capital must remain available and cannot be released without a lawful board resolution.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment approval letter
Company name and business scope pre-approval certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Inward remittance receipt and foreign-exchange settlement certificate
Bank statement showing the paid-in capital
CPA engagement letter and capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the remittance code, provide the investment permit and a copy of the business-scope certificate, or ask the remitter to amend the payment instructions with a corrected description. If the CPA cannot verify because the funds are un-cleared, the company must wait for final clearing and then obtain a supplementary bank certificate before filing the verification report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration Filing with the Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan - One-Stop Company Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed company registration application in the official system after the capital verification report is issued. The filing must attach the approved Articles of Incorporation signed by the founder or shareholders, the first board resolution, the Investment Commission permit, the name pre-approval certificate, the capital verification report, proof of registered-office address, and the identification and appointment documents of the director, supervisors and statutory officers. The Department will review legal-name compliance, scope legality, capital verification and officer eligibility. Once approved, the Company Registration Certificate and a unique company identification number are issued, and the company then has separate legal personality. All attachments should be in PDF form and submitted simultaneously to prevent a suspension; pay the statutory registration fee online.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application Form
Articles of Incorporation signed by shareholders
First Board of Directors Resolution
CPA capital verification report
Investment Commission foreign investment permission
Company name and business scope pre-approval certificate
Registered office lease or ownership proof and landlord consent
Passports and appointment letters for directors and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried, the Department usually issues a correctable defect notice; the applicant has 14 days to submit a conclusive correction. If registration is denied, the foreign shareholder may appeal under the administrative appeal procedure within 30 days, or after the appeal is exhausted, file an administrative action with the Taipei High Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice Number, Customs and Employer Post-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance for tax and invoices; Customs Administration for importer registration; Bureau of Labor Insurance for employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and business tax registration at the National Taxation Bureau having jurisdiction over the registered office, and obtain the Uniform Invoice Number. Register for electronic invoice and e-invoice platform services because the business will collect credit-card and bank-wire payments from B2B customers. If the entity will directly import MRO hardware, register as an importer with the Customs Administration and appoint an authorized customs broker. If the entity expects to hire staff, complete the labor insurance, health insurance and pension-account employer registrations. Present the Company Registration Certificate and tax documents to the bank to activate the operational account. Retain the registration certificates, tax registration card, and uniform invoice authorization in the statutory corporate record book.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Articles of Incorporation and board minutes
Tax registration application
Registered office and responsible person identification
E-invoice contract and service provider consent
Importer registration form if direct import of MRO goods
Employer registration forms if hiring employees
Company chop and banking mandate forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Taxation Bureau issues a tax-registration deficiency notice, supplement the missing tax information and endorsed company forms within 15 days. If the uniform invoice issuing certificate is delayed, the tax bureau should issue an interim invoice-use permission; delayed customs registration may be cured by refiling under the customs declaration and importer-registration procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is not registered for physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations; if it later operates an in-house warehouse, the competent municipal authority would be the local Bureau of Economic Development together with the Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory industrial operating permit is triggered by ISIC 4791 electronic catalog retail of industrial MRO supplies; the general tax and business registration certificates issued in Step 5 are the only operating permits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - for future physical operations, the agency would be the Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration and the local municipal environmental protection bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA at formation because only electronic-catalog retail and e-commerce are operated; a future warehouse or processing or assembly facility may require an Environmental Impact Assessment Category B or Category C depending on floor area and processes, or an environmental site registration under the EIA Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable at formation. If the entity later owns or operates a warehouse with a wash bay, stationary air pollution sources or hazardous waste, it must comply with the Water Pollution Control Act effluent standards, the Air Pollution Control Act VOC and stationary-source emission limits, and the Waste Disposal Act manifest and disposal requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at formation since there is no physical plant. If the entity later occupies a warehouse or fulfillment center, the following clearances become mandatory: Fire Safety Facility Inspection and Installation Certificate, Civil Defense Fire Safety Management Plan, building structural load inspection for racking and shelf loads, Fire Department approval of storage layout, and Occupational Safety and Health Administration site hazard assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online filing is conducted through the National Electronic Tax Bureau e-Tax portal at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn and the applicable provincial e-Tax platforms operated under STA supervision.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the PRC WFOE: (1) incorporate with the State Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code, which is the statutory Tax Identification Number for all PRC tax purposes; (2) within 30 days of issuance of the business license, complete the initial tax registration through the provincial e-Tax platform by submitting the articles of association, business license, registered office lease, legal representative identity documents, and the Taiwan shareholder's identity/certification of non-resident status; (3) the in-charge STA office then activates the taxpayer master file, determines small-scale or general VAT taxpayer status, and assigns electronic invoice quotas; (4) for export trade, register export-tax-rebate qualification with the same office or at first export declaration. For the non-resident shareholder entity itself, no PRC TIN is generally required unless it creates a permanent establishment or derives PRC-sourced income; if withholding registration is needed, the WFOE registers the non-resident shareholder in the e-Tax system and obtains a non-resident taxpayer code for withholding tax vouchers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None as an income-tax entity election. The PRC has no check-the-box or flow-through classification for a WFOE; a WFOE is mandatorily classified as a PRC resident enterprise taxed at entity level. For indirect tax administration only, a taxpayer below the general taxpayer threshold may elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer to claim

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), which serves as the Central Bank of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China maintains a regulated partial-convertibility FX regime: current account items (trade in goods and services, dividend remittances, and ordinary operating payments) are generally convertible at banks upon documentary verification, while capital account items (foreign direct investment, cross-border financing, and securities investment) remain subject to SAFE registration, filing, and in some cases prior approval. For this Taiwan-funded WFOE, the B2B MRO e-commerce receipts from overseas buyers fall under the goods trade foreign exchange supervision framework: the company must join the Trade Foreign Exchange Receipts and Payments Online Catalogue as an A-Category enterprise, and banks will settle trade receipts without per-transaction authorization provided the trade background is verifiable through customs declarations, contracts, invoices, and logistics records. Export proceeds enjoy 100 percent retention in foreign currency accounts; no mandatory surrender or conversion obligation exists under current SAFE rules. Profit remittances to the Taiwan shareholder are permitted only after the registered capital is fully injected and verified, the Chinese CPA annual audit is filed, corporate income tax and dividend withholding are settled, and the bank verifies the prior-year audited results; this creates a practical remittance hurdle of two to four weeks of documentation processing. Capital account inflows require a SAFE Foreign Investment registration with the settlement bank before the injection, and the funds must enter a designated capital escrow account; conversion of the capital into CNY is allowed for genuine business operating expenses and is prohibited for speculative securities or entrusted loans under the Foreign Investment Negative List. Overall, CNY convertibility for current-account operating flows is high, while capital-account convertibility is medium-high only when the WFOE sustains a flawless compliance documentation trail.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Since the 2012 SAFE reform and the current Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Administration Guidelines, no mandatory surrender ratio applies: exporters may keep 100 percent of export receipts in their foreign currency current account. The overriding statutory duty is timely repatriation: all export foreign exchange proceeds for goods actually exported from China must be collected into a domestic goods trade FX account within 180 days from the customs export declaration date, extendable to 390 days after a formal filing to the local SAFE branch for valid commercial causes. On receipt, the A-Category enterprise may either retain the foreign currency or settle into CNY at the bank spot rate; the bank reports the transaction under the goods trade balance-of-payments codes and matches it against the customs electronic data. Delinquent collection beyond the statutory window triggers a downgrade to B-Category status, which imposes per-transaction verification and a heavier documentary burden on all subsequent trade receipts and payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Capital Injection) plus Basic Operational RMB/FX Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Deposit Account plus Goods Trade FX Receipts and Payments Current Account
E-commerce Collection Settlement Account plus Corporate Online Treasury Interface
Cross-Border RMB Settlement Account plus Operating Expense RMB Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary treasury rail. European or Singapore-licensed EMI and neobank platforms cannot open domestic RMB current accounts or obtain CNY clearing membership in mainland China, and they are legally barred by PBOC and SAFE from acting as the receiving bank for SAFE-registered FDI capital injection or from performing capital-account FX settlement. Cross-border e-commerce payment service providers holding a PBOC Payment Business License may provide offshore card collection in USD or EUR, but the ultimate liquidity must be repatriated into the WFOE domestic goods trade FX account under the trade supervision framework. Therefore, the blueprint permits a licensed PSP for card acquiring only and mandates a Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank for all capital and trade settlement rails; the overall viability rating for EMIs as account providers is Low and as payment facilitators is Medium.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PBOC rules for the RMB basic deposit account require that the legal representative complete a face-to-face identity verification, either by appearing physically in-branch or, for a Taiwan shareholder holding a valid Taiwan Compatriot Permit, through the bank enterprise mobile video-KYC flow using the company Electronic Business License and corporate chops. Full remote opening is accepted only in pilot free-trade zones such as Shanghai FTZ for low-risk A-Category profiles; at all other branches a designated mainland financial manager must attend in-branch with the original company seal, financial seal, and legal representative chop to collect the bank package. Consular proxy opening is not accepted for a mainland basic deposit account, although a notarized power of attorney certified through the cross-strait notarization channel allows an authorized mainland officer to open the account while the Taiwan director acknowledges remotely by video; the WFOE should budget for one physical attendance by the mainland finance principal and one remote video acknowledgement by the Taiwan director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder chain opacity: Taiwan-resident investors hold the WFOE through a private intermediate holding company, preventing the bank from completing the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) matrix required by PBOC AML regulations; incomplete identification blocks basic deposit account activation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) notarized Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs company registration extract showing the complete holding chain to the ultimate natural persons; (ii) Taiwan ID and passport copies of each UBO plus their signed non-PEP and non-sanction declarations; (iii) the mainland business registration certificate of the WFOE; (iv) the SAFE FDI FX registration form; (v) an organizational chart signed and stamped by all directors listing indirect ownership percentages and a source-of-wealth narrative for the initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering suspicion: high-frequency low-value electronic catalog MRO transactions produce an invoice-and-order pattern that the compliance officer cannot promptly distinguish from split shipments or dual-invoicing into the cross-strait corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) 24-month platform order-level export extract with order ID, SKU, price, and buyer legal identity; (ii) matching commercial invoices and packing lists; (iii) forwarder bills of lading and air waybills with customs Electronic Port declaration numbers; (iv) a CPA agreed-upon procedures report reconciling a random 60-transaction sample of orders to bank receipts; (v) the e-commerce refund policy and chargeback log.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed card acquiring for cross-border B2B MRO sales: if the WFOE settles overseas buyer cards through a foreign acquirer without a PBOC Payment Business License, the bank may view the settlement as circumventing China cross-border payment supervision and refuse to book the wire receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) signed acquiring agreement with a licensed third-party payment institution holding the PBOC Payment Business License or with UnionPay International network member infrastructure; (ii) PCI-DSS compliance and penetration test certificates; (iii) monthly clearing and settlement statements reconciling card proceeds, foreign exchange conversion, and net settlement to the WFOE; (iv) a written opinion from Chinese counsel confirming that the acquiring structure does not violate cross-border payment rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection profile mismatch: early credits on the escrow account do not match the registered capital schedule in the articles, triggering a suspicious transaction report on equity capital arriving in small tranches rather than as one scheduled SWIFT wire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) the WFOE articles of association with a contribution timetable; (ii) the Ministry of Commerce foreign investment filing certificate and the SAFE FDI registration record annotated with the scheduled amount; (iii) a signed shareholder resolution committing that all capital contributions will be remitted exclusively by SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes matching direct investment; (iv) a bank-issued account transaction narrative for the first 12 months; (v) the CPA capital verification report issued after the first tranche.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before any remittance, the WFOE completes SAFE direct-investment FX registration with the receiving Tier-1 bank and obtains the Foreign Exchange Business Number for the FDI capital escrow account; the Taiwan shareholder then dispatches a SWIFT MT103 to that account, with the payment narrative quoting the WFOE name and the SAFE direct-investment purpose code for equity capital injection. The receiving bank validates the purpose code, credits the escrow account, and permits conversion into CNY only for lawful operating purposes under the Foreign Investment Negative List, uploading the capital account data to the SAFE system. The WFOE simultaneously retains a licensed Chinese CPA to perform statutory capital verification once the funds clear, producing the capital verification report required for updating the registered capital in the State Administration for Market Regulation corporate registry. Any change in the investment schedule, repatriation of excess funds, or a shareholder loan facility must be separately re-registered; using a fintech EMI or a credit-card top-up for capital injection would be rejected by the bank and would constitute a compliance violation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the B2B MRO export model, outbound liquidity clears through the China goods trade framework: the WFOE must be listed in the Trade FX Collection and Payment Catalogue as an A-Category enterprise at the settlement bank, and each disbursement is matched against the contract, commercial invoice, packing list, and transportation document. Low-value open-account supplier payments to Taiwan or third-country sources of MRO hardware are executed by SWIFT MT103 with settlement in one to two banking days; bulk consignments are transported via a documentary commercial letter of credit (MT700 or MT707) or a documentary collection (DP or DA) when the supplier requests bill-drawee protection; and cross-border Chinese yuan settlement through the CIPS system is available onshore to reduce FX conversion cost for Taiwanese suppliers accepting CNY. Chargebacks and refunds arising from credit-card e-commerce returns must be sourced from the acquiring institution refund rail and re-credited to the original card; if a refund must be made outside that rail, the WFOE issues an MT103 current-account refund with the chargeback reference, platform order number, and original card transaction audit trail. All payments are reportable to SAFE via the bank balance-of-payments return, and the WFOE must maintain A-Category status by avoiding overdue collection and irregular splitting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB/USD and RMB/TWD outright forwards with the SAFE real-demand principle: the underlying confirmed trade order, invoice, and customs declaration must be presented at trade execution
RMB foreign exchange swaps with a matched current-account timing gap for treasury working capital management, limited to the maturity of the underlying receipts or disbursements
Vanilla over-the-counter RMB call and put options for protective hedging of confirmed trade orders, exercisable only on genuine trade exposure

Cross-border RMB settlement through CIPS as a currency-neutral alternative that removes FX mismatch, and offshore CNH deliverable forwards executed by the Taiwan parent outside the Chinese capital account fence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) financial statement approval and shareholder resolution minute
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (Taiwan Company Registration Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end; for a calendar-year company by 30 June. May be extended by MOEA upon application for up to one additional six-month period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold an AGM within the statutory window permits the competent authority to call the meeting at the company's expense; responsible directors are subject to administrative fines of NT$20,000 to NT$100,000 (approx. USD 640–3,200), and continued non-compliance may trigger administrative dissolution/involuntary strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Profitable Enterprise Income Tax settlement return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (Taiwan local tax administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 May to 31 May following the close of the calendar tax year, or within five months after the close of a special fiscal year, unless the Ministry of Finance extends the filing period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a surcharge under the Tax Collection Act, plus monthly default interest at the central bank deposit rate; intentional non-filing can lead to tax assessment, penalty of up to 3 times the understated tax, coercive execution on assets, and ultimately administrative deregistration/strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CPA-audited annual financial statements (if statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders/AGM; filed with MOEA as part of the annual corporate registry record; no separate government filing fee for the audited report itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Draft financial statements must be submitted to directors no later than three months before the AGM (by 31 March for calendar-year), and the audited report must be presented at the AGM by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have a required CPA audit renders the financial statements non-compliant; MOEA may impose registration fines, directors/managers may incur penalties, and if the omission is used to evade tax, additional tax and penalties will be assessed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of directors, supervisors, managers, and 10-percent-or-more shareholders (Company Act Article 22-1 register update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) through the national company registration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any change in director, supervisor, manager, or shareholder holding 10% or more of issued shares; no separate fixed annual filing or 30-day transfer window is prescribed; the register must reflect the current position as of each year-end and be available for inspection.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the Article 22-1 register within 15 days exposes the company to administrative penalties per non-filing event, and may cause corporate registration matters to be rejected; recurring omissions can be enforced up to the stage of administrative dissolution/strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20, a non-public limited company is compulsorily required to have its annual financial statements audited and certified by an independent licensed CPA if its paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approx. USD 1 million). There is no separate statutory audit trigger based solely on turnover or headcount for ordinary non-public trading/e-commerce companies; however, public companies, financial holding companies, banks, securities, insurance, and other enterprises designated by the central competent authority are audited regardless of size. If the enterprise applies for financing or foreign-investment approval requiring audited statements, the MOEA or Investment Commission may additionally require a CPA report.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS (TIFRS) for public/publicly-listed and designated enterprises; for non-public companies, the Commercial Accounting Act and generally accepted accounting principles in Taiwan (ROC GAAP/TIFRS-based small-and-medium guidance) apply. Tax filings must be reconciled to the statutory financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no annual UBO confirmation form in Taiwan. The mandatory protocol is event-driven: any change in directors, supervisors, managers, or a shareholder's reach of 10% or more of issued shares must be reported to MOEA within 15 days. Shareholding transfers that cause a person to move above or below the 10% threshold are reportable in that 15-day window, not on a 30-day or annual cycle. For AML purposes, the corporate record must also identify a beneficial owner and controlling person, and the register must be made available to inspection by authorities on demand.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,200 per year (approx. NT$9,000–36,000), depending on registered agent and services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–20,000 per audit for a Taiwan non-public trading/e-commerce company meeting the NT$30 million paid-in-capital threshold (higher for group consolidated audits)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Retained earnings surtax of 5% applies to undistributed profits; no statutory patent box but R&D expenses qualify for a 100% deduction plus an additional 20% tax credit; enterprises operating in designated free-trade zones or offshore digital services hubs may enjoy reduced rates or investment tax credits for logistics automation and innovation in B2B MRO e-commerce platforms; export sales are zero-rated for VAT but remain fully subject to corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ROC Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form No. 75) filed electronically via the National Tax Administration e-Filing Portal (eTax); authenticated financial statements and TP report must be uploaded simultaneously for non-resident cross-border transactions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 5 months after fiscal year-end (by May 31 for calendar-year enterprises); a provisional estimated tax payment is due on September 30, with an additional semi-annual installment on March 31 for large taxpayers; extension procedures require a written application before the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Sales, Services Revenue and Net Business Revenue — total consideration from B2B MRO catalog sales, freight income, platform access fees, and ancillary electronic commerce services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a Taiwan WFOE acts as a digital intermediary, allocate revenue under the Company Law and permanent establishment rules; export sales to overseas buyers are exempt from business tax but must be included here as taxable income; foreign-source digital services must be segregated to avoid double counting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of Goods Sold — industrial MRO supplies purchased globally, inbound logistics, warehousing, direct labor, and overhead consumed in generating the gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases from the China parent or its affiliates must be priced at arm's length; if the CUP or resale price method is used, the enterprise must keep transfer pricing documentation ready; failure to substantiate inventory costs may trigger an automatic TP adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Profit — the arithmetic difference between Box 1 and Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile gross margin with internal divisional profit statements; if the Taiwan WFOE receives a marketing or procurement commission from the China parent, ensure that revenue is booked in Box 1 and no re-invoicing arrangement is used to shift profits out of Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Expenses — selling, general, administrative, technology, cloud infrastructure, and royalty payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to a non-resident licensor are deductible only if a 20% withholding tax is discharged (or treaty-reduced); failing to withhold renders the expense non-deductible; platform subscription and software fees must be classified as royalties or service charges consistently under the arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating Income and Expenses — exchange gain/loss, interest income, dividend income, and other residual items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest received from a China parent intercompany loan is taxable interest under the Income Basic Tax Act; if the interest is paid by a foreign borrower and no Taiwan PE is present, a foreign tax credit may be claimed only after the funds are remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income and Tax Computation — deduction of loss carryforwards, exemptions, and the application of the statutory 20% rate; also the computation of the 5% retained earnings surtax on undistributed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must compute taxable income based on the full amount as reported; the retained earnings surtax is triggered only when profit is not distributed by the end of the following year; if the shareholder is a Chinese resident, the distribution is subject to 21% statutory withholding unless a treaty relief process is explicitly approved and documented before the filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 3% of unpaid tax per month up to 30% if filed after the due date but before a tax assessment; up to 60% if filed after assessment; per Article 108 of the Tax Collection Act; a surcharge on underpaid estimated tax at 1% per month; statutory concealment of income triggers a penalty of twice the underpaid tax; fraudulent evasion under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine not exceeding NT$50 million; additionally, false TP documentation attracts NT$30,000 to NT$100,000 per infraction and a 2x underpaid tax penalty under Article 114-1 of the Income Tax Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders; 10% for resident individuals (subject to imputation system mechanism).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend rate under a bilateral DTA or the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction; (ii) file Form 'Application for Tax Treaty Relief' with the National Tax Administration at least 3 weeks before the dividend distribution; (iii) provide a notarized Beneficial Ownership Certificate demonstrating the shareholder is the true owner, holds substantive operations in the resident state, and has no conduit or back-to-back arrangements; (iv) present audited financials and an economic substance questionnaire for the past 3 years; (v) expect an advance ruling letter which is valid for 5 years. If the Chinese parent fails to provide these, the 21% statutory withholding applies and the excess tax cannot be credited.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties paid to non-residents is 20%, with a reduced 15% rate for qualified foreign enterprises licensing copyright or patented technology used in Taiwan manufacturing; intercompany interest paid to a non-resident lender is subject to 20% WHT, but a 10% rate applies to certain bank deposits and short-term commercial paper; treaty rates may reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 10% for qualifying DTA partners, subject to the same TRC and beneficial ownership protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$50 million in aggregate related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File preparation; NT$200 million in aggregate related-party transactions triggers Master File; Country-by-Country Report threshold is group consolidated revenue above NT$27 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies the Economic Substance Doctrine through Article 43-4 of the Income Tax Act and the Tax Transparency and Anti-Tax Avoidance Act; a WFOE in the B2B MRO e-commerce sector must show actual management, personnel, logistics infrastructure, and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Taiwan, such as order processing, risk assumption, inventory control, pricing strategy, and procurement negotiation; if the China parent exercises substantial decision-making, the WFOE may be treated as a shell, and its profits will be re-attributed to the resident party; the CIGA analysis must be embedded in the Master File and updated annually.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cross-border e-commerce revenue generated on the Taiwan WFOE platform and routing sales through an undisclosed PRC treasury account without an arm's length service agreement or TP record; issuing false invoices to conceal taxable revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Tax Collection Act, a penalty of twice the underpaid tax is assessed, in addition to the underpaid tax itself; criminal prosecution under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act (Tax Evasion) carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to NT$50 million; an arrest warrant may be issued for absconding taxpayers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil under Article 25 of the Company Act and Article 23 of the Tax Collection Act, making directors personally and jointly liable for the company's unpaid taxes and penalties; personal assets, bank accounts and private properties are frozen; directors are subject to a departure ban (blacklisting) preventing overseas travel; a criminal conviction imposes imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years, plus disgorgement of evaded assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a paper WFOE in Taoyuan with no physical offices, employees, or inventory, routing all contracts through a Hong Kong shelf company to claim treaty benefits or shift profits to the China parent; no supervision of local logistics and no risk-bearing capability in the MRO supply chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 43-4 of the Income Tax Act and the Tax Transparency and Anti-Tax Avoidance Act, the tax authority may re-characterize the entire revenue as directly derived by the China parent and assess tax on a deemed basis; treaty benefits are denied and a retroactive reassessment for up to 10 years is authorized; a penalty of 2 to 4 times the deficient tax is imposed depending on intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are treated as 'beneficial owner' claimants under the General Anti-Avoidance Doctrine; they become jointly and severally liable for the recaptured tax and surtax; the National Tax Administration can issue a restraining order on personal property and a travel restriction; criminal exposure under the Company Act's false reporting provision leads to imprisonment of up to 7 years and a fine of NT$20 million, plus mandatory corporate deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a 50% royalty to the China parent for generic catalog software without any underlying IP-bearing R&D or license agreement; pricing intercompany procurement below the adjusted TNMM interquartile range; failing to file a TP report or providing false comparability data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 114-1 of the Income Tax Act, a TP adjustment results in a penalty equal to 2x the underpaid tax; failure to prepare a TP report carries a fine of NT$30,000 to NT$100,000; if the TP report is falsified, the penalty escalates to 3x underpaid tax and criminal liability under the Commercial Accounting Act and Securities Crime Act; tax authorities may also impute unrealized profit based on the profit split method.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation commit perjury and falsification of financial records under Article 71 of the Commercial Accounting Act, carrying a sentence of 3 to 10 years imprisonment and a fine of NT$5 million to NT$50 million; they are personally liable for the recaptured tax and incurred penalties; assets, shareholdings and trust investments are subject to freezing; the director may be prohibited from serving as a director of any company in Taiwan for a period of 5 years.
